title: Seasonal sunrise terms changed bird survey-end temperature slopes by less than 0.003 taxa per 5 C in four Canada and US samples
abstract: We tested whether seasonal sunrise terms changed a published link between end temperature and last-minus-first recorded bird richness. Four Canada and US samples in 1985-2024 used 64,513 accepted surveys. We added a latitude-based sunrise shift, its square, and its products with start time and duration to fixed-effect models. Changes in the temperature slope ranged from -0.0022 to +0.0024 taxa per 5 C. All four adjusted intervals for the change included zero. US slopes stayed negative in both periods. Canada slopes remained uncertain. Fair-weather and route-date checks gave small changes. These terms describe seasonal sunrise changes, not absolute time since dawn. The result does not remove all timing bias or identify a causal heat effect. Selected visits, endpoint weather, fixed route order and shared records limit inference.

display.caption: End-temperature slopes with baseline controls and added seasonal sunrise terms. Bars are intervals adjusted for four country-period tests. The response is last-minus-first ten-stop recorded taxa.

citations.reason: Uses its verified panel, fixed-effect code, raw retrieval and panel build method. Records overlap before the sunrise screen. Tests a new seasonal timing explanation.
